categories.label: Bahia: Salvador, then the coast
categories.note: The first choice. Majority-Black, dry in January, and Os is already there.

categories.label: Colombia: Medellín, then the coffee region
categories.note: Welcoming by most Black travellers’ accounts, the cheapest, and one stop for each of us.

categories.label: Costa Rica: San José, then Manuel Antonio
categories.note: Animals everywhere, marriage equality, and a nonstop for Jabari. The rental budget is tight.

categories.label: Uruguay: Montevideo, then the Rocha coast
categories.note: Calm, very gay-friendly, and home of candombe. Pricey, and few accounts from Black visitors.

categories.label: Panama: Panama City, then Bocas del Toro
categories.note: Strong Afro-Caribbean presence and easy flights. The weakest on LGBTQ rights.

categories.label: Buenos Aires, and Colonia across the river
categories.note: The strongest city and gay scene, the least nature, and the most reports of staring.

categories.label: Chile: Valparaíso, then the Elqui Valley
categories.note: The best skies and the penguins, and the least comfortable fit for Jabari right now.

items.name: The Pelourinho and MUNCAB
items.blurb: The old upper city, pastel houses and gold-lined churches on cobbled hills, and MUNCAB, the museum of Afro-Brazilian culture, on Rua das Vassouras. On Sunday morning Olodum rehearses on the Largo do Pelourinho for free.
facts: MUNCAB is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 17:00
The Elevador Lacerda links the upper and lower city
Pickpockets on the side streets

items.name: The Lavagem do Bonfim
items.blurb: Salvador’s biggest religious festival outside Carnival falls inside our dates. Baianas in white walk about 8 km from Conceição da Praia to the Bonfim church and wash its steps, with the whole city behind them.
facts: Huge crowds and heat, so little to carry
The Bonfim ribbons are tied on with three wishes

items.name: Porto da Barra at sunset
items.blurb: The calm swimming beach below the Barra lighthouse, and the city’s sunset ritual, around 18:07. Porto da Barra and Buracão are the gay-friendly beaches.
facts: Busy at weekends
Barra is the flat, walkable part of the city

items.name: Acarajé and Rio Vermelho
items.blurb: Acarajé from Dinha on the Largo de Santana, then Rio Vermelho’s bars. For one proper dinner, moqueca at Casa de Tereza, about R$200–280 for two.
facts: Busiest Thursday to Saturday
Rideshare rather than walking after dark

items.name: Boipeba
items.blurb: An island with no cars, south of Salvador: a beach walk to the Moreré pools at low tide, a boat around the island, lobster at the beach shacks, and a dark sky for stars.
facts: Ferry, van and speedboat, 5 to 6 hours from Salvador
Island tax about R$70–90 each
No LGBTQ scene here, and small towns notice more

items.name: Sea turtles at Praia do Forte
items.blurb: Projeto TAMAR, the turtle conservation centre, in a village 50 minutes from the airport. Hatchlings emerge from November to March, and Reserva Sapiranga’s forest trails are five minutes away.
facts: Open 11:00 to 17:00, but the days vary, so worth checking
Releases are not on a fixed schedule

items.name: Medellín and the Metrocable
items.price: Metro about COP 4,400, Arví line about COP 26,700
items.blurb: Spring weather all year in a valley city that climbs its hillsides by cable car. Laureles is the flat, walkable, residential part to stay in, with Carrera 70 for food. The Metrocable’s Line L runs on up to Parque Arví, pine and cloud forest at the top.
facts: Around 25°C by day, 17°C at night, short afternoon showers on about half the days
Laureles apartments about $45–80 a night
Line L to Arví is closed every Tuesday
App taxis at night rather than street taxis

items.name: Comuna 13 with Casa Kolacho
items.blurb: The hillside neighbourhood that remade itself with murals and outdoor escalators. Casa Kolacho, the hip-hop collective that started the tours, has the artists guide it themselves, which is the respectful way to go.
facts: Starts at San Javier metro
Buying food and drinks from the stalls is part of it
Asking before photographing people

items.name: Guatapé and El Peñol
items.price: About COP 60,000 each, bus and climb
items.blurb: A granite dome rising out of a lake district two hours east of the city, with 702 steps to the top and the whole flooded valley below. Guatapé, the town beside it, is painted in bright friezes.
facts: Buses every 30 minutes from Terminal Norte, about 2 hours
The climb is COP 35,000
Worth avoiding 9 to 11 January, the Reyes long weekend

items.name: The Cocora valley
items.blurb: Wax palms, the tallest palms on earth, standing in green hills above Salento. The loop is 12–15 km through forest and pasture, and it is best started early, when the mornings are clearest.
facts: Willys jeeps from Salento’s plaza from about 6:30, COP 5,000 each way
Several private farms charge along the way, in cash
The last jeep back is around 18:30

items.name: Hummingbirds at Acaime
items.duration: An hour, on the Cocora loop
items.blurb: A small reserve about an hour up the forest side of the Cocora loop, with feeders that draw dozens of hummingbirds at once. The entry includes a hot chocolate with cheese in it, the way it is served here.
facts: On the loop, so it goes with the Cocora day
A dawn birding walk near Salento is the other way to see them

items.name: Salento and a coffee farm
items.blurb: The small town the coffee region runs through, painted in bright balconies. Finca El Ocaso, about an hour’s walk downhill, shows coffee from bush to cup with English tours at 9:00, 11:00, 13:00 and 16:00; Don Elías next door is the smaller family version.
facts: Around 21°C by day and 13°C at night, with some showers
A finca a few kilometres out is quieter, with birds and stars, about $60–140 a night
Café Jesús Martín in town for the coffee itself

items.name: Filandia, and the hot springs
items.price: Lookout about COP 12,000, springs about COP 86,000
items.blurb: Filandia is the quieter, prettier town nearby, with a lookout tower that is at its best at sunset. The Santa Rosa de Cabal hot springs, a waterfall-fed pool about 1.5–2 hours away, are a slow weekday.
facts: Local jeeps run between the towns
The springs run booked 4-hour shifts at weekends, so a weekday is easier

items.name: San José: the theatre and the market
items.price: Theatre tour ₡3,500, Gold Museum about US$16
items.blurb: The Teatro Nacional’s hourly tours and café, the gold museum under the plaza next door, then a casado at a Mercado Central soda for about ₡3,500–4,500. Barrio Escalante is the leafy part to stay and eat in.
facts: Theatre tours on the hour, 9:00 to 16:00
Market stalls are cash only, and busy with pickpockets
Poás volcano is closed

items.name: Toucan Rescue Ranch
items.blurb: A rescue centre for toucans, sloths and owls in the hills above San José, walked with a guide. The animals are ones that cannot go back to the wild.
facts: Booking ahead only
30 to 40 minutes from Escalante by Uber

items.name: Manuel Antonio National Park
items.blurb: Rainforest down to white beaches, with sloths, capuchins and iguanas. A guide, about US$30–40 each, is how the sloths get found. Kids Saving the Rainforest, a sanctuary ten minutes away, is the other animal morning, at US$60.
facts: Timed tickets online only, selling out 3 to 4 weeks ahead
Closed Tuesdays
No food or plastic bottles inside

items.name: Isla Damas mangroves by kayak
items.blurb: A paddle through mangrove channels near Quepos, with white-faced monkeys, crabs, herons and sometimes caimans.
facts: Timed by the tides
Usually includes pickup and a meal

items.name: Ciudad Vieja and the Mercado del Puerto
items.blurb: The old town on its peninsula, the 1868 iron market hall full of grills, Teatro Solís, and the carnival museum on the rambla. The Mercado Agrícola is the cheaper lunch.
facts: Ciudad Vieja empties after dark
Museo del Carnaval, Tuesday to Saturday, UYU 200

items.name: Candombe in Barrio Sur
items.blurb: Afro-Uruguayan drumming, and the heart of the country’s carnival. The groups set out from Isla de Flores y Ansina on Sunday afternoons, with the drums audible blocks away.
facts: Sundays from about 16:00
The big Llamadas parade is in February, after we leave

items.name: The Rambla to Pocitos
items.blurb: Seven kilometres of waterfront from the old town to Pocitos, on foot or by bike, with the city out on it on a summer evening. Sunset is around 20:00.
facts: No shade and a strong wind
City beaches sometimes get algae warnings in summer

items.name: Cabo Polonio
items.blurb: A village on the dunes with no roads and no grid power, reached by 4x4 truck. Hundreds of sea lions lie on the rocks below the lighthouse in summer, and with no lights the sky is very dark.
facts: About 4h30 by bus from Montevideo, then 20 to 30 minutes by truck
Rustic, and busy with day-trippers
Lighthouse closed Mondays

items.name: Santa Teresa and Punta del Diablo
items.blurb: A national park of woods and palm-lined beaches with an 18th-century fortress, ten kilometres from the fishing village of Punta del Diablo. Laguna de Rocha, with flamingos and black-necked swans, is a day trip.
facts: Fortress 10:00 to 18:00 in season, pesos only
Local buses are infrequent; taxis fill the gaps

items.name: Casco Viejo and Black Panama
items.price: Museum free with a reservation, not confirmed
items.blurb: The old town on its point, with the fish market’s US$1–4 ceviche. A walking tour, Black History: Shadows and Lights, runs from Plaza Herrera to the Afro-Antillean Museum, telling the story of the West Indian canal workers.
facts: The museum is closed Mondays, and its hours vary between sources
Sunset drinks at Gato Blanco, a gay-friendly rooftop

items.name: The canal at Miraflores
items.blurb: The visitor centre over the Miraflores locks, where ships the size of buildings rise and fall a few metres away.
facts: Open to 18:00
Ship transits are not scheduled for visitors

items.name: Pipeline Road, Soberanía
items.price: Free to walk, by most reports
items.blurb: A flat 17 km track through rainforest 45 minutes from the city, where dawn brings toucans, monkeys and coatis. Monkey Island on Gatún Lake, by boat from about US$30, is nearby.
facts: Minivan from Albrook, US$2 each way
The far section is closed

items.name: Bocas del Toro by boat
items.blurb: The Caribbean islands: Dolphin Bay, the reefs at Coral Cay, the Zapatilla cays and sloths in the mangroves. Old Bank on Bastimentos is the Afro-Caribbean village, with rondón, a fish and coconut soup.
facts: Air Panama from the city, US$170–215 each way
The sea decides whether Zapatilla happens
Rain on about half of January days

items.name: Boca del Drago and Starfish Beach
items.blurb: A bus across Isla Colón, then a 20-minute shore walk to a beach where starfish sit in the shallows.
facts: Starfish are for looking at, not lifting
Last bus back at 18:00
Crowded around midday

items.name: Palermo and San Telmo
items.blurb: Palermo is the default: leafy, walkable, most of the food and the bars, and the parks of the Bosques close by. San Telmo is older, cobbled and cheaper, with the Sunday fair along Defensa from 10:00 and Pride Café, the city’s first openly gay café, on the corner.
facts: About 28°C by day, often over 30, and about 7 rain days in January
The hottest hours, 14:00–17:00, are for being indoors
Paying by foreign card now gets close to the best rate; cash no longer pays

items.name: Recoleta and El Ateneo
items.blurb: The Recoleta cemetery is a city of marble family tombs, Evita’s among them. El Ateneo Grand Splendid, a short walk away, is a 1919 theatre turned bookshop, with a café where the stage was.
facts: Cemetery daily 9:00–17:00, about ARS 25,000 for visitors
El Ateneo open late, to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays
A good pair for the hot afternoon hours

items.name: Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur
items.blurb: Wetland reclaimed from rubble on the river’s edge, right behind Puerto Madero’s towers: reed beds, herons, swans, coots and nutria, and paths out to the water. The nature half of a city week, a walk from the centre.
facts: Tuesday to Sunday 8:00–19:00 in summer, closed Mondays
Closes on rainy or very windy days
No shade, so early is better

items.name: The Tigre delta
items.blurb: A maze of brown rivers and islands north of the city, with houses on stilts, rowing clubs and a boat for every errand. The train from Retiro takes 50 minutes; the shared Interisleña boat does the rest.
facts: Train about ARS 450, the boat ARS 5,000 return
Boat times shift with the tides and the day
The Puerto de Frutos market is busiest at weekends

items.name: Colonia del Sacramento
items.blurb: Across the river in about an hour: a small cobbled Portuguese town on a point, quiet once the day-trippers leave at five. Staying overnight is the version worth having.
facts: Colonia Express is usually cheaper than Buquebus, which can pass $100 in January
Booking the ferry a month or two ahead
Old-town apartments about $65–125 a night

items.name: Valparaíso’s hills
items.blurb: A port stacked up forty-odd hills, painted end to end with murals, with Cerro Alegre and Cerro Concepción as the walkable middle of it. The free walking tour leaves Plaza Sotomayor at 10:00 and 15:00 and runs on tips, which is the easy way into the place on the first day.
facts: Around 13–21°C and dry, with cool evenings
Cerro Alegre and Concepción are where to stay, about $50–90 a night
El Internado on Cerro Alegre is a relaxed mixed bar

items.name: The ascensores
items.blurb: The old funicular lifts that haul people up the hills, some running since the 1880s. Seven were working in 2026, Reina Victoria and Concepción among them, 7:00 to 21:30. Riding a few of them is most of a morning well spent.
facts: Locals pay CLP 200–300; visitors CLP 1,000
Lifts close for repairs without notice, so it is worth checking on the day

items.name: La Sebastiana, and the sea lions
items.blurb: Neruda’s tall, odd house on Cerro Bellavista, built like a ship’s bridge over the bay, with an English audioguide. Down the coast at Caleta Portales, sea lions lie about next to the fish stalls, and a train or a bus along the shore to Viña del Mar costs under CLP 1,000.
facts: Closed Mondays; Tuesday to Sunday 10:00–19:00 in summer
No booking, first come first served
Fried fish and seafood empanadas from the Portales stalls

items.name: Santiago
items.blurb: Two hours inland by bus. The funicular up Cerro San Cristóbal for the whole city with the Andes behind it, the zoo on the way, La Vega Central for a market lunch, and Bellavista in the evening for dinner and a drag show. Teatro a Mil, a big theatre festival, runs 3 to 24 January.
facts: Around 30°C and very dry
Funicular about CLP 2,250 return; the zoo CLP 4,000 and closed Mondays
Farinelli in Bellavista has drag from about 23:00, Tuesday to Sunday
Lastarria is the walkable place to stay

items.name: The Elqui Valley
items.blurb: A dry green valley of vineyards and pisco villages under bare mountains, clear 92% of the time. Pisco Elqui is the prettiest place to stay, by the river; Vicuña is the working town where the observatory tours start. River walks, swimming spots, long lunches, and then the nights.
facts: Around 25–30°C by day and 16°C at night
A one-hour flight from Santiago to La Serena, then about an hour’s bus up the valley
A car for 3 or 4 days opens up the upper valley, from about $30 a day

items.name: Stargazing at Mamalluca
items.blurb: Some of the clearest skies anywhere, which is why the big observatories are up here. Mamalluca, above Vicuña, runs public night tours with telescopes, including one in English. Sunset is around 20:50, so the stars start about 22:00.
facts: Sells out in January, so booking online early matters
The new moon is 7 January and the full moon the 22nd, so the first week is darkest
Transport from Vicuña is extra; the observatory is about 9 km out

items.name: Pisco distilleries
items.duration: Half an hour to an hour
items.blurb: Pisco comes from this valley. Los Nichos, from 1868, is the oldest distillery in Chile and still small; Pisco Mistral, in the middle of Pisco Elqui, is the polished version with tastings.
facts: Los Nichos is about 3.5 km out, daily 10:00–18:00
Pisco Mistral tours at 12:00, 14:00 and 16:00

items.name: Humboldt penguins at Isla Damas
items.duration: A full day from La Serena
items.blurb: A boat out to the Humboldt Penguin reserve: penguins on the rocks, sea lions, otters, and often bottlenose dolphins alongside. About 3 hours on the water with an hour ashore.
facts: Boat CLP 30,000, park fee CLP 7,400, bus CLP 4,500 each way
The reserve lands visitors Wednesday to Sunday only
Swell can cancel boats, so a spare day helps
No fuel on the Punta de Choros road, for anyone driving
